name: Dortmund Airport
before:
Dortmund's airport, 10 km east of the city, serving the eastern side of the Rhine-Ruhr, Germany's largest urban area. It is mostly low cost and leisure charter flying and carried nearly 3 million passengers in 2023.

Onward travel has two good options and it is worth knowing both. An express bus runs to Dortmund main station, from which frequent regional and long distance trains reach Düsseldorf. Alternatively a shuttle leaves the terminal every twenty minutes for Holzwickede station, where the hourly RE 13 runs direct to Düsseldorf in about an hour. There are also buses to the U47 metro line and to Unna.

Düsseldorf Airport, the region's main one, is about 70 km to the south west.

The airport has a long history in two places. Commercial flights began in 1925 from a field at Brackel, with Aero Lloyd flying to Paris, but that site became a German air base in the war and was held by British forces until the 1990s. The civil airfield moved to Dortmund-Wickede in 1960.
after:
Dortmund's airport, 10 km east of the city and the third busiest in North Rhine-Westphalia, with just over 3.2 million passengers in 2025. Most of its flying is low cost, with Wizz Air the biggest airline and many routes to Central and Eastern Europe.

Onward travel has two good options. The AirportExpress bus runs to Dortmund main station, and the AirportShuttle to Holzwickede station, where the RE 13 runs direct to Düsseldorf. There are also buses towards the U47 metro line and to Unna.

Düsseldorf Airport, the region's main one, is about 70 km to the south west.

The airport has a long history in two places. Commercial flying began at Brackel in 1925, when an Aero Lloyd aircraft was the first to land, but the military took the site over in 1939 and it later passed to British forces. Flying moved to the present site at Dortmund-Wickede in 1960.

claims.inAfter: Most of its flying is low cost, with Wizz Air the biggest airline and many routes to Central and Eastern Europe.

The routes are mostly not holiday charters: Eurostat's 2024 figures (the latest by route) have Katowice, Bucharest, Gdansk, Tirana, Sofia and Skopje among the seven busiest, with Palma the one leisure route near the top. Wizz Air flights fill most of the airport's current timetable (its name appears 547 times, against 113 for SunExpress and 99 for Eurowings), and Wikipedia calls it the biggest contributor to the airport's growth.

claims.claim: leisure charter flying; nearly 3 million in 2023
claims.wasBefore: It is mostly low cost and leisure charter flying and carried nearly 3 million passengers in 2023.

claims.claim: frequent regional and long distance trains from Dortmund main station to Dusseldorf
claims.wasBefore: An express bus runs to Dortmund main station, from which frequent regional and long distance trains reach Düsseldorf.
claims.why: The onward trains to Dusseldorf rest on Wikipedia alone (the operator says only that both stations are on Deutsche Bahn's regional and long distance network). The express bus is kept (see above).

claims.claim: the shuttle every twenty minutes; the hourly RE 13 in about an hour
claims.wasBefore: Alternatively a shuttle leaves the terminal every twenty minutes for Holzwickede station, where the hourly RE 13 runs direct to Düsseldorf in about an hour.
claims.why: The operator's own timetable has the shuttle every 20 minutes only on weekday daytimes (every 30 at weekends and in the evening), and the RE 13's hourly frequency and journey time rest on Wikipedia alone. The shuttle and the direct RE 13 are kept (see above).

claims.claim: Aero Lloyd flying to Paris; British forces until the 1990s
claims.wasBefore: Commercial flights began in 1925 from a field at Brackel, with Aero Lloyd flying to Paris, but that site became a German air base in the war and was held by British forces until the 1990s.
claims.why: The Paris route and 'until the 1990s' rest on Wikipedia alone; the operator's centenary history has the first aircraft arriving from Bremen and the British from 1958. Corrected (see above).

claims.claim: the express and shuttle buses do not take VRR tickets
claims.why: Held back: a practical warning that replaces nothing, from the operator alone: neither bus is part of the VRR network, so local public transport tickets are not valid (Rail&Fly tickets are accepted on the shuttle but not on the express).
